title: Why do wings diverge where they diverge? Causal decomposition of the Thompson-7 skew in hornet (30 spp, ~30 Myr) and bee (42 tribes, ~110 Myr) forewings
motivation: Thompson (1917, pp. 385-386) proposed, and never carried out, 'a mathematical study of ... the deformation of the wing ... from one species to another'. His own reading of such deformations was causal: form as the record of forces acting during growth. The descriptive results (vespinae_wings, bee_wings) found that the 7 a-priori global grid modes carry 39% of between-species variance in hornets but 56% of between-tribe variance in bees, with the unexplained residual central in hornets and at the base/apex in bees. This registration asks what produces that skew. Four causal accounts are separable with data already in hand, because both datasets have replicate wings per unit (so a pooled within-unit covariance matrix P, the 'developmental/individual' channel, can be estimated) and the hornet data have a size proxy.

causal_accounts.A_measurement: The residual pattern is where landmarks are imprecisely placed, not where biology is. Prediction: per-landmark within-unit variance tracks the per-landmark T7-residual fraction.
causal_accounts.B_channelled_drift: Divergence is neutral-ish accumulation along the directions in which individuals already vary (Schluter 1996 'lines of least resistance'; Hansen & Houle 2008). Prediction: among-unit divergence is aligned with p_max of P far more than chance; Brownian motion on the tree with rate matrix proportional to P reproduces the observed T7 share and the observed residual location.
causal_accounts.C_allometry: Global grid change is a by-product of size evolution (Thompson's own default explanation, cf. his horse-skull and Aceratherium series). Prediction (hornets only): log centroid size explains a substantial share of among-species shape variance, and the allometric direction is more T7-loaded than divergence in general.
causal_accounts.D_function: Selection for flight mechanics shapes the grid independently of P and size. Not directly testable here; it is the residual account if A-C fail, and the sign of C3/C4 (observed T7 share ABOVE what P-drift gives) is the diagnostic that something beyond channelled drift pushes variance into the global modes.

hypotheses.statement: The per-landmark fraction of among-unit variance NOT captured by T7 is NOT predicted by per-landmark within-unit variance (Spearman rho <= 0.5 or p >= 0.05). I.e. the residual pattern is not a digitising artefact.
hypotheses.note: Bee landmarks 1-18 include 41 wings from literature drawings; base/apex landmarks are plausibly the least repeatable, which is why the bee prior is lower.

hypotheses.statement: Among-unit divergence is aligned with the within-unit covariance structure: the angle between d_max (leading eigenvector of the among-unit covariance) and p_max (leading eigenvector of pooled within-unit P) is below the 5th percentile of random-direction angles in the tangent space, AND the first 3 within-unit PCs carry more than twice the random-expectation share of among-unit variance.
hypotheses.note: Channelled drift should be strongest for shallow divergence (hornets), where there has been less time for selection to move lineages off the P ridge.

hypotheses.statement: Brownian motion on the group's tree with rate matrix proportional to P (plus sampling error P/n_u at the tips) reproduces the observed T7 variance share: the observed share lies inside the central 90% of 2000 simulated shares.
hypotheses.note: Registered expectation: bees will sit ABOVE the simulated band (deep divergence is more global than P-drift predicts), hornets inside it. If bees are above, accounts C/D are needed for the deep-time Thompsonian pattern.

hypotheses.statement: The same simulation reproduces the observed residual location: the observed ratio (mean unexplained fraction at the 10 long-axis-end landmarks) / (mean unexplained fraction at the middle landmarks) lies inside the central 90% of simulated ratios.
The within-unit covariance P is itself less Thompsonian than among-unit divergence: the T7 share of trace(P) is at least 10 percentage points below the T7 share of among-unit variance.
hypotheses.note: If true for bees but not hornets it says deep divergence is concentrated into the global modes relative to the developmental channel, i.e. the skew is produced over time, not inherited from P.

hypotheses.statement: Evolutionary allometry is substantial: log centroid size (pixel, single-lab imaging; species order validated against known body sizes before registration) explains >= 15% of among-species shape variance (multivariate regression, permutation p < 0.05).

The allometric direction is more Thompsonian than divergence in general: the T7 share of the size-regression vector exceeds the overall among-species T7 share (0.388) by at least 10 percentage points.
hypotheses.note: Thompson's reading of the grid as a growth record predicts that size-correlated change is global.

hypotheses.statement: Removing allometry removes the Thompsonian signal: the T7 share of size-corrected residual shape is at least 5 percentage points below the uncorrected share.

protocol.units: as registered for each group (species on the Open Tree induced subtree for hornets; tribes with >= 3 wings on the dated tribe tree for bees)
protocol.tangent_space: all wings GPA-aligned together; unit means re-aligned to the consensus M0 by OPA; D = unit means minus M0 (n x 2K); within-unit deviations W = wing minus its unit mean in the same frame; P = pooled within-unit covariance (sum of SSCP / (N_wings - n_units))
protocol.T7: eng.thompson_mode_basis(M0) as in all previous runs
protocol.C1: per-landmark unexplained fraction fr_j (as B6/W7) vs per-landmark within-unit variance (trace of the 2x2 block of P); Spearman rho, two-sided p
protocol.C2: angle acos(|d_max . p_max|); null = 2000 random unit vectors in R^(2K) projected out of the 4 similarity directions; 'share of among-unit variance on first 3 within PCs' vs random expectation 3/(2K-4)
protocol.C3_C4: C = MRCA-height matrix of the kept tips (eng.Tree.C); X_sim = L_C G L_P^T + tip noise with cov P/n_u, G iid N(0,1), 2000 reps; statistics: T7 share of X_sim (centred), ends/middle unexplained-fraction ratio with the same end-landmark sets as the descriptive runs (N_END = 5 per end)
protocol.C6_C8: hornets: y = log median centroid size per species; multivariate regression D ~ y (Procrustes ANOVA R^2, 5000 permutations); allometric vector = slope row; size-corrected D = residuals
protocol.reporting: all statistics for both groups regardless of outcome; Brier over registered probabilities; interpretation written after the run and labelled as such

what_would_change_my_mind: If C1 fails in bees (residual tracks digitising noise) the base/apex result is withdrawn as biology. If C3 passes in bees, the deep-time Thompsonian pattern needs no explanation beyond drift along P and the 'Thompson describes deep divergence' claim is reinterpreted as 'P is Thompsonian and time integrates it'. If C6/C7 pass, Thompson's growth-record reading of his own grid gets its first direct support in this programme.
